Class SlotElement

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.element.AbstractPanelElement
com.trevlar.slotkit.api.slot.SlotElement
All Implemented Interfaces:
com.trevlar.menukit.api.element.PanelElement
public final class SlotElement extends com.trevlar.menukit.api.element.AbstractPanelElement
A registered slot shown as a PanelElement. A slot is just another element you put in a panel, next to buttons and labels.

What this element does, and what it doesn't

A slot has two separate parts:
  • Registration: a real, server-synced CreatedSlot in menu.slots, built when the menu is constructed through CreatedSlots. This class doesn't touch it.
  • Placement: where it sits on screen, which is what SlotElement owns. Each frame, in layer 2 of ContainerScreenLayers (after vanilla has drawn the vanilla slots and before it draws the created ones), it converts its panel-relative position to screen space and writes it into the live slot's own Slot.x/y. It also draws the recessed 18x18 frame, which is panel chrome.
It does not draw the item, count, durability bar, hover highlight or ghost icon. Vanilla does: its extractSlots walks menu.slots and draws this slot at the x/y written here, through the same extractSlot call it uses for a vanilla slot, and its getHoveredSlot finds it the same way. So a third party's slot hook, or any mod reading slot.x/y, treats a created slot and a vanilla slot the same, because SlotKit has no separate slot pass for them to differ in. CustomContainerScreen has always worked this way on its own screens.

In a clipping container

In a ScrollContainer (or anything else that clips what it draws) the slot scrolls and clips like any element. Each frame it places its slot, it reports it to MenuKit (SlotClip.shown) with the clip it draws under, and MenuKit holds vanilla's draw of the slot and its hover to that clip: a slot across the viewport's edge keeps its position and shows, hovers and takes clicks only inside. A slot wholly out of view is not rendered, so it is parked (below).

Vanilla slots

SlotElement.Builder.slot(Address) presents a vanilla slot instead: one the menu built itself, named by Address.menuSlot(MenuType, int) (the same slot on every menu of a type, which is what a panel registered once wants) or by the container-based address SlotRef.address() gives (one particular box). The slot keeps everything vanilla gives it (sync, shift-click, its category); the panel only moves it. Its position changes only on screens where this element is attached: there it sits where the panel puts it, or parked when the panel doesn't show it, and every other screen's layout is untouched. A screen's background still draws the slot's old frame at its old spot, so a panel taking over a vanilla grid hides that. Present each vanilla slot at most once per screen, and never as a created slot over the same container as well, which would put two views of one container in menu.slots.

Looked up each frame, not held

A SlotElement holds no slot reference. It holds the slot's stable Address and looks up the live in-menu slot from the current screen's menu each frame, through CreatedSlotAdapter's cache. That is what lets one panel registered once work on every screen. The survival inventory and the creative screen carry different slot instances for the same logical slot (creative wraps it in a SlotWrapper on a throwaway menu), and a held reference would be wrong on one of them. The position is written to whichever instance is in menu.slots, the wrapper on creative, because that is the one vanilla draws.

Parked when not shown

At the end of each frame (SlotElementRegistry.parkUnpresented(AbstractContainerMenu)), every attached element whose panel did not render it that frame moves its slot off-screen. So a slot whose panel is hidden, out of its region, or hidden by the window sits where vanilla neither draws nor hit-tests it next frame, instead of where it was last drawn. A slot that was shown keeps its position, so hover between frames matches what is on screen. (CreatedSlot.isActive() handles a hidden panel by itself; parking handles the other cases.)

Several panels may hold the same slot, each gated by visibleWhen (one layout on survival's inventory, another on creative's): the panel shown this frame places it, and it parks only when none did. Two shown at once both write it, and SlotKit warns, since the slot can only be in one place.

A vanilla slot parks only while its element is shown but out of view (scrolled out of a ScrollContainer or a region, which MenuKit reports through renderCulled). While the element or its panel is hidden, or once the screen closes, it goes back to where the menu put it, so a mod that hides its panel hands the slot back to vanilla's layout.

MenuKit lays out every panel before vanilla's slot pass and draws each panel's slots right after the panel (7.3.0), so a slot in an overlay or popover panel draws on it, in the same frame.

Why a slot stays live under its own panel

Vanilla owns a slot's item interaction: AbstractContainerScreen.mouseClicked calls slotClicked(getHoveredSlot()), and MenuKit's getHoveredSlot interception (CreatedSlotInput) makes the registered slot win over a vanilla slot it covers. An opaque panel claims its whole rectangle with no holes, so the claim sends a point over this element's slot back to vanilla (presentsSlotAt(InputContext)). The panel's own slot hovers and takes clicks, while anything else under the panel stays inert. On a transparent panel the slot is not solid (isElementOpaque() is false), so it claims nothing itself. SlotElementRegistry tells the library's screen hook which panels currently host a SlotElement.

    • builder

      public static SlotElement.Builder builder()
      A slot element: SlotElement.builder().slot(CreatedSlots.groupId(panel, group), i).at(x, y).build(). The usual element methods apply: at, visibleWhen (on top of the slot's own reveal), and tooltip (shown over an empty slot; a slot with an item shows the item's). A slot is never solid, so opaque has no effect.

    • panelId

      public @Nullable String panelId()

    • hostedVanillaSlot

      @Internal public @Nullable net.minecraft.world.inventory.Slot hostedVanillaSlot(net.minecraft.world.inventory.AbstractContainerMenu menu)
      The vanilla slot this element hosts on menu when it placed the slot in the last frame, else null. A slot parked, or back at its own place while the panel is hidden, isn't hosted: there it must not win hover over a created slot a shown panel puts on that spot. Always null for a created slot.
